critical.issue: iter29 RCA fix (res.headers.append('Set-Cookie', ...) twice) did NOT split the Set-Cookie headers on the wire. Wire output (verified with both curl --http1.1 -i and curl HTTP/2 -i) is still a single 'set-cookie:' line: 'admin_premfa=; Path=/; HttpOnly; SameSite=Lax; Max-Age=0, admin_token=<JWT>; Path=/; HttpOnly; SameSite=Lax; Max-Age=86400'. Browser parses only first cookie → admin_token never set → all admin pages redirect to signin. RECOMMENDED FIX: stop emitting two Set-Cookie headers entirely. Drop the admin_premfa-clear from this response — admin_premfa already has Max-Age=600 so it self-expires; or rely on subsequent middleware/route logic to prefer admin_token over admin_premfa. Emit ONLY 'admin_token=<JWT>; Path=/; HttpOnly; SameSite=Lax; Max-Age=86400' in this response. This eliminates the merge-collision entirely.

critical_code_review_comments: headers.append('Set-Cookie', ...) called twice in NextResponse does NOT guarantee two separate Set-Cookie headers on the wire when the response transits Cloudflare HTTP/2. Verified empirically here: curl --http1.1 -i still shows one merged header line, and the browser cookie jar gets only the first cookie. The Web Fetch Headers spec says Set-Cookie should be the only header that doesn't combine, but the runtime + proxy chain in this preview env collapses them anyway.

Robust fix: avoid the dual-Set-Cookie scenario altogether. Drop the explicit clear of admin_premfa in the verify-mfa response — its Max-Age=600 (~10 min) is short enough that it self-expires harmlessly, and any auth-priority logic should already prefer admin_token over admin_premfa.

If clearing admin_premfa immediately is required, do it via an HTTP 302 redirect (browser follows, sends a separate request that the redirect target can use to clear the cookie), or move the clear into a middleware that runs on the next admin page hit.

rca of the issue: Main agent applied the iter29 RCA recommendation: replaced NextResponse.cookies.delete(ADMIN_PREMFA_COOKIE) + NextResponse.cookies.set(ADMIN_TOKEN_COOKIE, ...) with two res.headers.append('Set-Cookie', '...'). However, empirical testing in this iter (curl --http1.1 -i, curl HTTP/2 -i, AND Playwright real browser) shows the wire still emits ONE 'set-cookie:' header line containing both cookies merged with a comma. Either the Next.js 16 runtime serializes Headers.append('Set-Cookie', ...) by joining values, or Cloudflare's edge proxy is collapsing them at HTTP/2 framing. Browsers (and curl cookie-jar) parse only the first cookie of a merged 'admin_premfa=...; Max-Age=0, admin_token=...' line, so admin_token is dropped. Mitigation: emit ONLY ONE Set-Cookie in this response — for admin_token. Drop the explicit admin_premfa clear since it already has Max-Age=600 and self-expires. This sidesteps the merge-collision entirely. Verify with `curl --http1.1 -i` and Playwright's document.cookie.
